message.content:
This is a CBP ruling on the Nomad XL body panel and chassis assembly. The question is whether to classify it as an incomplete vehicle under 8703 (GRI 2(a)) or as parts under 8708.

The assembly has no motor, no battery, no steering wheel, no wheels and no brakes, so it lacks essential features of a complete vehicle. Under GRI 2(a), an incomplete vehicle is classified as a complete one only if it has the essential character of the complete vehicle. A chassis with a body, but without the engine, is classified under heading 8707 (bodies) or 8708 (parts) rather than 8703. Heading 8706 covers chassis fitted with engines, so it does not apply here.

Heading 8707 covers bodies, including cabs, for the motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705. The assembly here combines a chassis and a body. A chassis with body but without the engine would typically fall under 8708.29 (other parts and accessories of bodies) or 8708.99 (other parts). In earlier rulings, a body and chassis assembly without a powertrain has been placed in 8708.99.8180 or 8708.99.68.

Golf carts are classified in 8703.21, and low-speed vehicles are classified in 8703.80 (electric). The body-and-chassis unit is a part of those vehicles, and the parts provision at 8708 covers parts of the vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705. A golf cart is in 8703, so 8708 applies. For the statistical suffix, the choice was 8708.99.8180 ("other parts, other"), and I am going with that one.

{"hts_code": "8708.99.8180", "reason": "The unpowered body-and-chassis platform lacks the motor, battery, wheels and steering wheel, so it is not an incomplete vehicle of heading 8703 under GRI 2(a), and it is classified as an 'other part' of a motor vehicle in heading 8708."}

predicted_reason: The unpowered body-and-chassis platform lacks the motor, battery, wheels and steering wheel, so it is not an incomplete vehicle of heading 8703 under GRI 2(a), and it is classified as an 'other part' of a motor vehicle in heading 8708.
